body: Root cause: the Codex plugin stops its broker only from a Claude SessionEnd hook, and git-hook reviews run outside any Claude session, so each review leaves a broker tree running (about 150 MB or more). BewareILive's codex-review has the same shape. Fix on VectorCraft's hooks branch: (1) after each review, stop the broker whose --cwd is that review's tree and all its descendants (TERM, then KILL); (2) `codex-review reap` at runner start, for brokers whose review tree is gone, limited to the project's own prefix; (3) a test with a fake detached broker. With branch reviews it's one broker per branch, not one per commit. Commit hash to follow. Suggested for both xtask doctors: flag leftover brokers and high swap at session start.
summary: Broker leak: root cause and the shared .githooks fix for BewareILive to copy
